# DokoDash

> DokoDash is a web-first 2D platformer inspired by Nepal's harvest paths, festivals, wildlife, Himal routes, and Kathmandu rooftops. The canonical public site is https://dokodash.app/.

## Canonical URLs

- [Play DokoDash](https://dokodash.app/): Official production game.
- [Staging](https://staging.dokodash.app/): QA and preview environment for upcoming changes. Do not treat staging as canonical content.

## Project Summary

DokoDash is a browser-playable Nepal-themed platformer built as a fast web vertical slice. Players choose a hero, collect rice, avoid hazards and enemies, use Nepali food powerups, and clear a five-route map across Nepal-inspired locations.

The game is currently focused on proving the vertical slice, mobile playability, route variety, leaderboard safety, and shareable web deployment before larger art or app-store expansion.

## Heroes

- Bir, Terrace Scout: safer first-clear hero with four hearts and a longer Dal Bhat Strength powerup.
- Asha, Himal Runner: faster hero with double jump and a longer Momo Dash powerup.

## Routes

- Khet Terrace, Ilam: hillside terrace-field route and first playable level.
- Festival Run, Tansen: festival route with route-specific hero attire and setpieces.
- Terai Wilds, Chitwan: lowland wildlife route with Terai styling and hazards.
- Everest Ascent, Solukhumbu: Himal route with snow, ascent pressure, and Yeti hazards.
- Kathmandu Roofs, Kathmandu: rooftop route with moving platforms and Kathmandu finish art.

## Gameplay Notes

- Collectible rice grains act as coins and scoring pickups.
- Powerups include momo, sel roti, and dal bhat from overhead doko baskets.
- Enemies include scarecrow, bird guardian, Yeti, and Kathmandu route hazards.
- Desktop controls use keyboard movement and jump keys.
- Mobile controls use touch movement, jump controls, and responsive HUD overlays.
- The leaderboard is moderated server-side for infeasible scores, repeated invalid submissions, and abusive names.
- Player feedback can be submitted from inside the game with runtime context.
